verdict.rationale: First-party Open WebUI Computer docs show real coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Cline and others) running as native chat backends. A 'supervise a coding agent' flow shows every file read and edit, with Allow/Deny approvals, and parallel agents can each run on their own git worktree. Separate scheduled-task docs show prompts that run the test suite, which covers editing and testing in real repos. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of repo cloning, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the coding-agent integration.

support.subject: As a developer, the assistant can supervise or embed real coding agents so it does repo work — cloning, editing, testing — not just snippets in chat

citations.quote: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Cline, or Pi run as native chat backends using the CLI login already on your machine.
You see the full history: every file it read, every edit it made, and the pending approval that's blocking it, rendered as tool cards with Allow / Deny buttons.
one worktree per task, one workspace per worktree, one agent per workspace, all supervised from a single browser tab.
Schedule a task that runs the test suite every weekday at 9 and reports failures with the error output.
